# Format: the syntax description (`<command>.py`)

This file states the command's argument syntax: the options it accepts, the type of argument each
option takes, and the types of its operands. It is a Python module that defines one variable.
Downstream programs import the module and read that variable; they do not call anything else in it.

## Shape of the file

```python
from caruca.ir.syntax import *

<command>_syntax_spec: list[SyntaxSpecification] = [
    [                      # one syntax (a command may have several alternative syntaxes)
        [ ...option nodes... ],      # position 0
        [ ...positional nodes... ],  # position 1
    ],
]
```

- The file is named `<command>.py` and the variable is named `<command>_syntax_spec`. Both use the
  command's name, so `tee.py` defines `tee_syntax_spec`.
- All constructors come from the module `caruca.ir.syntax`.
- `<command>_syntax_spec` is a list of **syntaxes**. Each syntax is one way the command line can be laid
  out; most commands have exactly one.
- A syntax is a list of **positions**, in order. Each position is a list of **argument nodes** allowed at
  that position. In every sample, position 0 holds the option nodes and position 1 holds the positional
  operands.

## Argument nodes

An argument node is one constructor call. Two kinds exist.

**`Flag(flag, alias=[...])`** — an option that takes no value, such as `-v` or `--verbose`. The first
argument is the option's spelling; `alias` lists other spellings of the same option.

**Value nodes** — anything that carries a value. The constructor name states the kind of value (see the
vocabulary below). Keyword arguments:

| Keyword | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `flag="-m"` | The node is an option that takes a value, written `-m VALUE`. Omit `flag` and the node is a positional operand instead. |
| `alias=["--max-count"]` | Other spellings of the same option. |
| `flag_followed_by_equals=True` | The value is attached with `=`, as in `--interactive=always`. |
| `choices=["never", "once", "always"]` | The allowed values, for `Selection` and `String`. |
| `arity=Arity.<name>` | How many times this node may appear on the command line (see below). |
| `dash_as_stdin=True` | On `Path` only: a lone `-` in this position means standard input. |

`Integer` also accepts `min=` and `max=` (an inclusive value range) and `suffixes=(...)`.
`List` describes a separator-joined list of values and accepts `of=<value node type>` and `separator=","`.

## Arity

`arity` says how many times a node may appear, not how many values it takes. The default is `OPTIONAL`.

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Arity.OPTIONAL`, `Arity.ZERO_OR_ONE` | zero or one time (the default) |
| `Arity.EXACTLY_ONE` | exactly once |
| `Arity.EXACTLY_TWO` | exactly twice |
| `Arity.ZERO_OR_MORE` | any number of times, including none |
| `Arity.AT_LEAST_ONE`, `Arity.ONE_OR_MORE` | one or more times |

## Vocabulary of value nodes

Each name below is a constructor exported by `caruca.ir.syntax`. Names on the same line are the same type
under different names.

| Constructor | Value it stands for |
|---|---|
| `Path` | a file or directory path |
| `Integer`, `Int`, `Number`, `Pid`, `Duration` | an integer |
| `String`, `Other`, `User`, `Format` | free text; `Other` is the catch-all when nothing more specific fits |
| `Selection` | one value out of a fixed set given in `choices` |
| `List` | several values joined by a separator |
| `Regex` | a regular expression |
| `Glob` | a shell wildcard pattern such as `*.txt` |
| `Separator`, `Delimiter` | a delimiter string |
| `Char` | a single character |
| `Range` | a numeric range such as `1-2` or `1,3` |
| `Size` | a size with a unit suffix, such as `1k` or `1m` |
| `Permission` | a file permission such as `u+r` or `0755` |
| `OwnerGroup` | an `owner:group` pair |
| `Group` | a group name |
| `Signal` | a signal name or number |
| `Variable` | an environment variable name |
| `Command` | the name of another command |
| `Hostname` | a host name |
| `Filesystem` | a filesystem type such as `ext4` |
| `Date`, `DateTime` | a date or a date-time |
| `DateFormat` | a `strftime`-style date format |
| `TimeStyle` | a time style name such as `iso` or `full-iso` |
| `Expression` | an arithmetic expression |
| `PrintfFormat`, `SprintfFormat` | a `printf`-style format string |
| `Geometry` | a size or percentage such as `100x100` or `50%` |

# Format: the behaviour annotation, as PaSh consumes it

PaSh describes a command with three files. Together they let PaSh parse an invocation of the command,
work out which of its arguments are inputs and outputs, and decide whether the invocation's work can be
split across parallel copies. The files live in the `pash_annotations` Python package (the module
paths below are that package's), and the samples under `samples/*/annotation/` are copied from it unchanged.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `<command>.json` | the parser table: the command's flags and options, and the type of each option's argument |
| `InputOutputInfoGenerator<Command>.py` | a class that, given a parsed invocation, marks which operands and option arguments are read, which are written, and whether standard input and standard output are used |
| `ParallelizabilityInfoGenerator<Command>.py` | a class that, given a parsed invocation, lists the ways its work may be split and recombined; when the file is absent, PaSh treats the command as not parallelisable |

`<Command>` is the command's name with its first letter capitalised (`grep` → `Grep`).

## 1. The parser table, `<command>.json`

```json
{
    "flag": [
        ["-c", "--count"],
        ["-D"],
        "-f"
    ],
    "option": [
        ["-e", "PATTERNS"],
        ["--regexp", "PATTERNS"],
        ["-f", "--file", ["FILE", "CONFIG_INPUT"]]
    ]
}
```

- `flag` lists the options that take no argument. Each entry is a list of the spellings of one flag;
  the first spelling is the one the parser reports. A bare string is accepted as a one-spelling entry.
- `option` lists the options that take an argument. Each entry is one or more spellings followed by
  the argument's type name. The type name is free text taken from the manual (`NUM`, `WHEN`, `MODE`),
  except that a file argument is written as a two-element list, `["FILE", <access>]`, where `FILE`,
  `DIR` or `DIRECTORY` marks it as a path and `<access>` is one of the access kinds in section 4.
- Two spellings of the same option may be listed as separate entries (grep's `-e` and `--regexp`) or in
  one entry (`-f`, `--file`).

PaSh's parser reads an invocation left to right: words found in `flag` or `option` are collected, with
an option consuming the following word as its argument; a word of the form `-abc` whose letters are all
flags is split into them; the first word that is none of these starts the operand list.

## 2. The input/output class

```python
from pash_annotations.annotation_generation.annotation_generators.InputOutputInfoGenerator_Interface import InputOutputInfoGeneratorInterface


class InputOutputInfoGenerator<Command>(InputOutputInfoGeneratorInterface):

    def generate_info(self) -> None:
        ...
```

The class defines one method, `generate_info`. PaSh constructs the object with the parsed invocation,
calls `generate_info`, and reads the result. Before `generate_info` runs, every operand is already
marked as a streaming input and option arguments are already typed from the parser table; the method
changes what differs for this command and this invocation.

**Inspecting the invocation** (inherited):

| Call | Returns |
|---|---|
| `self.does_flag_option_list_contain_at_least_one_of(["-q", "-c"])` | whether any of the named flags or options is present |
| `self.get_flag_option_list_filtered_with([...])` | the present ones among those named |
| `self.get_operand_list_length()` | the number of operands |
| `self.get_first_operand_name_as_string()` | the first operand's text |
| `self.does_first_operand_start_with(s)`, `self.does_first_operand_contain(s)` | tests on that text |
| `self.cmd_inv.flag_option_list`, `self.cmd_inv.operand_list` | the parsed lists themselves |

**Declaring inputs and outputs** (inherited):

| Call | Effect |
|---|---|
| `self.set_implicit_use_of_stdin()` | standard input is read even though no operand names it |
| `self.set_implicit_use_of_stdout()` | standard output is written |
| `self.if_no_operands_given_stdin_implicitly_used()` | the first, only when there are no operands |
| `self.all_operands_are_streaming_inputs()` | every operand is a file read as a stream (the default) |
| `self.all_operands_are_streaming_outputs()` | every operand is a file written as a stream |
| `self.all_operands_are_other_inputs()` / `..._other_outputs()` | every operand is a file read, or written, in some non-streaming way |
| `self.all_but_last_operand_is_streaming_input()` / `..._other_input()` | the last operand is left for a separate call |
| `self.all_but_first_operand_is_streaming_input()` / `..._streaming_output()` / `..._other_input()` | the first operand is left for a separate call |
| `self.only_last_operand_is_stream_output()` / `..._other_output()` | the last operand alone is an output |
| `self.set_first_operand_as_config_arg_type_string()` | the first operand is not a file but a value, such as a pattern |
| `self.set_all_operands_as_config_arg_type_string()` | no operand is a file |
| `self.set_first_operand_as_config_arg_type_filename_or_std_descriptor()` | the first operand is a file read as configuration rather than as a stream |

## 3. The parallelizability class

```python
from pash_annotations.annotation_generation.annotation_generators.ParallelizabilityInfoGenerator_Interface import ParallelizabilityInfoGeneratorInterface


class ParallelizabilityInfoGenerator<Command>(ParallelizabilityInfoGeneratorInterface):

    def generate_info(self) -> None:
        ...
```

Again one method, `generate_info`, with the same inspection calls as above. It appends zero or more
**parallelizers** to a list. A parallelizer is a splitter, a mapper and an aggregator: how the input is
divided, what runs on each part, and how the parts' outputs are recombined. Appending nothing means the
invocation is not parallelised.

**Splitters:** `indiv_files` (each input file is its own part), `consec_chunks` (the input is cut into
consecutive pieces), `round_robin` (lines are dealt out to parts in turn).

**Mappers:** by default the same command runs on each part (`seq`). A custom mapper is named with
`make_mapper_spec_custom(name, is_implemented=...)` from
`pash_annotations.annotation_generation.datatypes.parallelizability.MapperSpec`.

**Aggregators:** `conc` (concatenate the parts' outputs in order; the default), `adj_lines_merge`
(merge the boundary lines of adjacent parts), `adj_lines_seq` (run the command itself over the boundary
lines of adjacent parts), `adj_lines_func` (a named function over the boundary lines), and custom
2-ary or n-ary functions. The `make_aggregator_spec_*` constructors live in
`pash_annotations.annotation_generation.datatypes.parallelizability.AggregatorSpec`; the ones that take
a function name also take `is_implemented`, and a name beginning `PLACEHOLDER:` marks a function PaSh
does not yet provide.

**Appending a parallelizer**, in two forms:

- The inherited one-call shortcuts, named `append_to_parallelizer_list_<splitter>_seq_<aggregator>`
  with splitter in `if`, `cc`, `rr` and aggregator in `conc`, `adjm`, `adjs`, `adjf`; the `adjf` ones
  take `(string_repr_func, is_implemented)`. Examples: `self.append_to_parallelizer_list_cc_seq_conc()`,
  `self.append_to_parallelizer_list_rr_seq_adjs()`.
- Building one explicitly with `make_parallelizer_consec_chunks(...)`,
  `make_parallelizer_round_robin(...)` or `make_parallelizer_indiv_files(...)` from
  `pash_annotations.annotation_generation.datatypes.parallelizability.Parallelizer`, each taking
  optional `mapper_spec`, `aggregator_spec` and `info_splitter_mapper` (an
  `AdditionalInfoSplitterToMapper` value: `NO_ADD_INPUT`, `LINE_NUM_OFFSET`, `BYTE_OFFSET`,
  `LINE_NUM_AND_BYTE_OFFSET`, for mappers that need to know where their part began), then
  `self.append_to_parallelizer_list(parallelizer)`.

`self.set_commutative()` records that the parts' outputs may be recombined in any order.

## 4. Access kinds

Used in the parser table's file-argument entries and behind the input/output calls above:

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `STREAM_INPUT` | a file read as the data stream the command processes |
| `CONFIG_INPUT` | a file read for configuration, such as a pattern file |
| `CONTAINER_FOR_INPUT` | a file that lists the real input files |
| `EXCLUDES_FROM_INPUT` | a file that lists what to leave out |
| `OTHER_INPUT` | read in some other way |
| `STREAM_OUTPUT` | a file written as the output stream |
| `OTHER_OUTPUT` | written, created or removed in some other way |

class ParallelizabilityInfoGeneratorGrep(ParallelizabilityInfoGeneratorInterface):

    # list_of_all_flags = ["-V", "--help", "-E", "-F", "-G", "-P", "-i", "--no-ignore-case", "-v", "-w",
    #                      "-x", "-y", "-c", "-L", "-l", "-o", "-q", "-s", "-b", "-H", "-h", "-n", "-T", "-Z",
    #                      "--no-group-separator", "-a", "-I", "-r", "-R", "--line-buffered", "-U", "-z"]
    # list_of_all_options = ["-e", "-f", "--color", "-m", "--label", "-A", "-B", "-C", "--group-separator",
    #                        "--binary-files", "-D", "-d", "--exclude", "--exclude-from", "--exclude-dir", "--include"]

    # Which ones do affect parallelizability?
    # -c, -L, -l, -b, -n;
    # by checking, -L and -l overrule -c overrule -b and -n; output of -n always precedes output of -b
    # assumption: RR not over file boundaries
    # and -A, -B, and -C but we do not parallelize within file boundaries since they require context
    # for -q, the input is not read further after some condition is met, so we do not parallelize at all
    # for -m, we only do IF

    def generate_info(self) -> None:
        if not self.does_flag_option_list_contain_at_least_one_of(["-q"]):
            # # for indiv files
            # self.append_to_parallelizer_list_if_seq_conc()
            # rest for round-robin
            mapper_spec = None
            aggregator_spec = None
            add_info_from_splitter = None
            # CA to decide which mapper or aggregator, parallelizer added after CA
            if not self.does_flag_option_list_contain_at_least_one_of(["-A", "-B", "-C", "-m"]):
                if self.does_flag_option_list_contain_at_least_one_of(["-L", "-l"]):
                    # the output for both options is either empty or the filename (same for both if so)
                    # for "-l": if there was a match in one part, the filename will propagate; if not, not
                    # for "-L": if there was no match in one part, the filename will propagate; it not, not
                    aggregator_spec = make_aggregator_spec_custom_2_ary_from_string_representation(cmd_inv_as_str='PLACEHOLDER:merge_keeping_longer_output',
                                                                                       is_implemented=False)
                elif self.does_flag_option_list_contain_at_least_one_of(["-c"]):
                    aggregator_spec = make_aggregator_spec_custom_2_ary_from_string_representation(cmd_inv_as_str='PLACEHOLDER:sum_indiv_results_up',
                                                                                       is_implemented=False)
                    # cat input1 input2 | paste -s -d + - | bc
                elif self.does_flag_option_list_contain_at_least_one_of(["-n"]) and self.does_flag_option_list_contain_at_least_one_of(["-b"]):
                    mapper_spec = make_mapper_spec_custom('PLACEHOLDER:grep_add_line_number_and_byte_offset',
                                                                     is_implemented=False)
                    add_info_from_splitter=AdditionalInfoSplitterToMapper.LINE_NUM_AND_BYTE_OFFSET
                elif self.does_flag_option_list_contain_at_least_one_of(["-n"]):
                    mapper_spec = make_mapper_spec_custom('PLACEHOLDER:grep_add_line_number_offset',
                                                                     is_implemented=False)
                    add_info_from_splitter=AdditionalInfoSplitterToMapper.LINE_NUM_OFFSET
                elif self.does_flag_option_list_contain_at_least_one_of(["-b"]):
                    mapper_spec = make_mapper_spec_custom('PLACEHOLDER:grep_add_byte_offset',
                                                                     is_implemented=False)
                    add_info_from_splitter = AdditionalInfoSplitterToMapper.BYTE_OFFSET
                else:   # none of the above affecting flags
                    pass    #just keep mapper and aggregator None and thus add RR_SEQ_CONC
            # we exploit that mapper_spec becomes seq and aggregator_spec becomes conc if given None
            # check can be removed once all are implemented! (exploits short-circuiting)
            # TODO: we should be able to remove the `is_implemented`-check as it is checked later
            if (mapper_spec is None or mapper_spec.is_implemented) and \
                    (aggregator_spec is None or aggregator_spec.is_implemented):
                parallelizer_cc = make_parallelizer_consec_chunks(mapper_spec=mapper_spec,
                                                                  aggregator_spec=aggregator_spec,
                                                                  info_splitter_mapper=add_info_from_splitter)
                self.append_to_parallelizer_list(parallelizer_cc)
                parallelizer_rr = make_parallelizer_round_robin(mapper_spec=mapper_spec,
                                                                 aggregator_spec=aggregator_spec,
                                                                 info_splitter_mapper=add_info_from_splitter)
                self.append_to_parallelizer_list(parallelizer_rr)

              write to FILE instead of stdout

              write as per the comma separated symbol list

       skip=N (or iseek=N) skip N ibs-sized input blocks

              The  LEVEL  of information to print to stderr; 'none' suppresses
              everything but error messages,  'noxfer'  suppresses  the  final
              transfer  statistics, 'progress' shows periodic transfer statis‐
              tics

       N and BYTES may be followed by the following  multiplicative  suffixes:
       c=1,  w=2,  b=512,  kB=1000,  K=1024,  MB=1000*1000, M=1024*1024, xM=M,
       GB=1000*1000*1000, G=1024*1024*1024, and so on for T, P, E, Z, Y, R, Q.
       Binary prefixes can be used, too: KiB=K, MiB=M, and so on.  If  N  ends
       in 'B', it counts bytes not blocks.

       ascii  from EBCDIC to ASCII

       ebcdic from ASCII to EBCDIC

       ibm    from ASCII to alternate EBCDIC

       block  pad newline-terminated records with spaces to cbs-size

       unblock
              replace trailing spaces in cbs-size records with newline

       ucase  change lower case to upper case

       swab   swap every pair of input bytes

       sync   pad  every  input  block  with  NULs to ibs-size; when used with
              block or unblock, pad with spaces rather than NULs

       excl   fail if the output file already exists

       nocreat
              do not create the output file

       notrunc
              do not truncate the output file

       noerror
              continue after read errors

       fdatasync
              physically write output file data before finishing

       fsync  likewise, but also write metadata

       append append mode (makes sense  only  for  output;  conv=notrunc  sug‐

              fail unless a directory

    # dict_option_to_class_for_arg: Dict[str, WhichClassForArg] = get_dict_option_to_class_for_arg(json_data)

    # parse list of command invocation terms
    flag_option_list: List[FlagOption] = []
    i = 1
    while i < len(parsed_elements_list):
        potential_flag_or_option = parsed_elements_list[i]
        if potential_flag_or_option == '': # empty string counts as an operand
            break
        if potential_flag_or_option in set_of_all_flags:
            flag_name_as_string: str = dict_flag_to_primary_repr.get(potential_flag_or_option, potential_flag_or_option)
            flag: Flag = Flag(flag_name_as_string)
            flag_option_list.append(flag)
        elif (potential_flag_or_option in set_of_all_options) and ((i+1) < len(parsed_elements_list)):

            option_arg_as_string: str = parsed_elements_list[i+1]
            option = Option(option_name_as_string, option_arg_as_string)
            flag_option_list.append(option)
            i += 1  # since we consumed another term for the argument
        elif are_all_individually_flags(potential_flag_or_option, set_of_all_flags):
            for split_el in list(potential_flag_or_option[1:]):
                flag: Flag = Flag(f'-{split_el}')
                flag_option_list.append(flag)
        else:

from pash_annotations.parser.util_parser import get_json_data


class InputOutputInfoGeneratorInterface(Generator_Interface, ABC):

    # here, we only need to specify information about operands and implicitly used resources
    # information about option arguments are provided by parsing infrastructure
    # ASSUMPTION: No implicit information should be exploited since internal implementation may change


    def __init__(self, cmd_invocation: CommandInvocationInitial) -> None:
        super().__init__(cmd_invocation=cmd_invocation)
        flagoption_list_typer: List[Union[Tuple[Literal[WhichClassForArg.FILESTD], AccessKind],
                                                    Tuple[Literal[WhichClassForArg.ARGSTRING], None],
                                                    Tuple[Literal[WhichClassForArg.PLAINSTRING], None]]] \
                                = self.get_flagoption_list_typer_for_specific_list()
        self.input_output_info: InputOutputInfo = InputOutputInfo(
                                                    flagoption_list_typer=flagoption_list_typer,
                                                    number_of_operands=len(cmd_invocation.operand_list)
                                                  )

    @abstractmethod
    def generate_info(self) -> None:
        pass

    def get_info(self) -> InputOutputInfo:
        return self.input_output_info

    def get_cmd_inv_with_io(self, cmd_inv: CommandInvocationInitial) -> CommandInvocationWithIO:
        return self.input_output_info.apply_input_output_info_to_command_invocation(cmd_inv)

    def get_flagoption_list_typer_for_specific_list(self) -> \
            List[Union[Tuple[Literal[WhichClassForArg.FILESTD], AccessKind],
                       Tuple[Literal[WhichClassForArg.ARGSTRING], None],
                       Tuple[Literal[WhichClassForArg.PLAINSTRING], None]]]:
        dict_option_to_class_for_arg: Dict[str, Union[Tuple[Literal[WhichClassForArg.FILESTD], AccessKind],
                                                      Tuple[Literal[WhichClassForArg.ARGSTRING], None]]] = self.get_dict_option_to_class_for_arg()
        flagoption_list_typer = []
        for flagoption in self.cmd_inv.flag_option_list:
            if isinstance(flagoption, Flag):
                flagoption_list_typer.append((WhichClassForArg.PLAINSTRING, None))
            elif isinstance(flagoption, Option):
                flagoption_list_typer.append(dict_option_to_class_for_arg[flagoption.get_name()])
            else:
                raise Exception("neither Flag nor Option")
        return flagoption_list_typer

    def get_dict_option_to_class_for_arg(self) -> Dict[str, Union[Tuple[Literal[WhichClassForArg.FILESTD], AccessKind],
                                                                  Tuple[Literal[WhichClassForArg.ARGSTRING], None]]]:
        dict_option_to_class_for_arg: Dict[str, Union[Tuple[Literal[WhichClassForArg.FILESTD], AccessKind],
                                                      Tuple[Literal[WhichClassForArg.ARGSTRING], None]]] = dict()
        json_data = get_json_data(self.cmd_inv.cmd_name)
        for option_data in json_data["option"]:
            option_name = option_data[0]
            option_arg_info = option_data[-1]
            # CA whether access info is given
            if isinstance(option_arg_info, list):
                option_arg_type: str = option_arg_info[0]
                option_arg_access_str: str = option_arg_info[1]
                access: AccessKind = get_access_from_string(option_arg_access_str)
                if option_arg_type in INDICATORS_FOR_FILENAMES:

                    dict_option_to_class_for_arg[option_name] = (WhichClassForArg.FILESTD, access)

                dict_option_to_class_for_arg[option_name] = (WhichClassForArg.ARGSTRING, None)
        return dict_option_to_class_for_arg

    # Assumption: (streaming) outputs are always filenames or stdout

        self.input_output_info.all_operands_are_streaming_inputs()

        self.input_output_info.all_operands_are_streaming_outputs()

from pash_annotations.parser.util_parser import get_json_data


def parse(command) -> CommandInvocationInitial:

    # split all terms (command, flags, options, arguments, operands)
    parsed_elements_list : list[str] = shlex.split(command)

    cmd_name: str = parsed_elements_list[0]
    json_data = get_json_data(cmd_name)
    # TODO: if there is an element "\n", we lose the quotation marks currently

    set_of_all_flags: Set[str] = get_set_of_all_flags(json_data)
    dict_flag_to_primary_repr: Dict[str, str] = get_dict_flag_to_primary_repr(json_data)
    set_of_all_options: Set[str] = get_set_of_all_options(json_data)
    dict_option_to_primary_repr: Dict[str, str] = get_dict_option_to_primary_repr(json_data)
    # dict_option_to_class_for_arg: Dict[str, WhichClassForArg] = get_dict_option_to_class_for_arg(json_data)

    # parse list of command invocation terms
    flag_option_list: List[FlagOption] = []
    i = 1
    while i < len(parsed_elements_list):
        potential_flag_or_option = parsed_elements_list[i]
        if potential_flag_or_option == '': # empty string counts as an operand
            break
        if potential_flag_or_option in set_of_all_flags:
            flag_name_as_string: str = dict_flag_to_primary_repr.get(potential_flag_or_option, potential_flag_or_option)
            flag: Flag = Flag(flag_name_as_string)
            flag_option_list.append(flag)
        elif (potential_flag_or_option in set_of_all_options) and ((i+1) < len(parsed_elements_list)):
            option_name_as_string: str = dict_option_to_primary_repr.get(potential_flag_or_option, potential_flag_or_option)
            option_arg_as_string: str = parsed_elements_list[i+1]
            option = Option(option_name_as_string, option_arg_as_string)
            flag_option_list.append(option)
            i += 1  # since we consumed another term for the argument
        elif are_all_individually_flags(potential_flag_or_option, set_of_all_flags):
            for split_el in list(potential_flag_or_option[1:]):
                flag: Flag = Flag(f'-{split_el}')
                flag_option_list.append(flag)
        else:
            break  # next one is Operand, and we keep these in separate list
        i += 1

    # we would probably want to skip '--' but then the unparsed command could have a different meaning so we'd need to keep it
    # for now, omitted
    # if parsed_elements_list[i] == '--':
    #     i += 1

    operand_list = [Operand(operand_name) for operand_name in parsed_elements_list[i:]]

    return CommandInvocationInitial(cmd_name, flag_option_list, operand_list)

                                                  )

            List[Union[Tuple[Literal[WhichClassForArg.FILESTD], AccessKind],
                       Tuple[Literal[WhichClassForArg.ARGSTRING], None],
                       Tuple[Literal[WhichClassForArg.PLAINSTRING], None]]]:
        dict_option_to_class_for_arg: Dict[str, Union[Tuple[Literal[WhichClassForArg.FILESTD], AccessKind],
                                                      Tuple[Literal[WhichClassForArg.ARGSTRING], None]]] = self.get_dict_option_to_class_for_arg()
        flagoption_list_typer = []
        for flagoption in self.cmd_inv.flag_option_list:
            if isinstance(flagoption, Flag):

            elif isinstance(flagoption, Option):
                flagoption_list_typer.append(dict_option_to_class_for_arg[flagoption.get_name()])

        return flagoption_list_typer

from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Set

from pash_annotations.annotation_generation.annotation_generators.InputOutputInfoGenerator_Interface import InputOutputInfoGeneratorInterface
from pash_annotations.datatypes.AccessKind import make_stream_input, make_stream_output, make_other_output
from pash_annotations.datatypes.BasicDatatypes import FileName
from pash_annotations.datatypes.BasicDatatypesWithIO import get_from_original_filename_with_ioinfo


class InputOutputInfoGeneratorDd(InputOutputInfoGeneratorInterface):

    # list_of_all_flags = ["--help", "--version"]
    # list_of_all_options = []   (none in the dash-style sense the parser understands)
    # key=value operands = ["bs", "cbs", "conv", "count", "ibs", "if", "iflag", "obs", "of", "oflag",
    #                       "seek"/"oseek", "skip"/"iseek", "status"]

    # dd has no positional operands: every word is KEY=VALUE. The parser cannot split these, so
    # they all arrive in the operand list and are parsed here. None of them is a file by itself,
    # so all operands become config strings; the files named by if= and of= are reported through
    # the implicit streaming input/output slots, which fall back to stdin/stdout when absent
    # (dd treats a lone '-' as a literal file name, not as a std descriptor).
    #
    # Which ones affect input/output?
    # if=, of=: choose the input and output file; the last occurrence of a key wins.
    # seek=/oseek= (non-zero), conv=notrunc, oflag=append: existing output data is kept, so the
    #   output file is modified rather than written as a stream -> OTHER_OUTPUT.
    # skip=/iseek=, count=: still a sequential read of (part of) the input -> STREAM_INPUT.
    # conv=excl/nocreat only constrain creation of the output; data is still streamed.
    # status= only touches stderr.

    @staticmethod
    def _split_key_value(word: str):
        if "=" in word:
            key, value = word.split("=", 1)
            return key, value
        return word, None

    def _parse_key_value_operands(self):
        last_value: Dict[str, str] = dict()
        list_symbols: Dict[str, Set[str]] = {"conv": set(), "iflag": set(), "oflag": set()}
        for operand in self.cmd_inv.operand_list:
            key, value = self._split_key_value(str(operand.get_name()))
            if value is None:
                continue  # dd rejects such a word; nothing to record
            if key == "oseek":
                key = "seek"
            elif key == "iseek":
                key = "skip"
            if key in list_symbols:
                list_symbols[key].update(s for s in value.split(",") if s != "")
            else:
                last_value[key] = value
        return last_value, list_symbols

    @staticmethod
    def _is_zero(value: Optional[str]) -> bool:
        if value is None:
            return True
        try:
            return int(value, 0) == 0
        except ValueError:
            return False

    def generate_info(self) -> None:
        # --help / --version print to stdout and touch no files; as in the other annotations we
        # assume they are not given, but handle them for completeness
        if self.does_flag_option_list_contain_at_least_one_of(["--help", "--version"]):
            self.set_all_operands_as_config_arg_type_string()
            self.set_implicit_use_of_stdout()
            return

        last_value, list_symbols = self._parse_key_value_operands()
        self.set_all_operands_as_config_arg_type_string()

        # input side
        if "if" in last_value:
            input_file = get_from_original_filename_with_ioinfo(FileName(last_value["if"]), make_stream_input())
            self.input_output_info.set_implicit_use_of_streaming_input(input_file)
        else:
            self.set_implicit_use_of_stdin()

        # output side
        output_is_modified_in_place = ("notrunc" in list_symbols["conv"]) \
            or ("append" in list_symbols["oflag"]) \
            or not self._is_zero(last_value.get("seek"))
        if "of" in last_value:
            access = make_other_output() if output_is_modified_in_place else make_stream_output()
            output_file = get_from_original_filename_with_ioinfo(FileName(last_value["of"]), access)
            self.input_output_info.set_implicit_use_of_streaming_output(output_file)
        else:
            self.set_implicit_use_of_stdout()

class ParallelizabilityInfoGeneratorDd(ParallelizabilityInfoGeneratorInterface):

    # list_of_all_flags = ["--help", "--version"]
    # key=value operands = ["bs", "cbs", "conv", "count", "ibs", "if", "iflag", "obs", "of", "oflag",
    #                       "seek"/"oseek", "skip"/"iseek", "status"]

    # Which ones affect parallelizability?
    # Without conversions dd is a byte-for-byte copy, so splitting the input into pieces, running the
    # same dd on each and concatenating the results gives the same bytes: CC/RR x SEQ x CONC.
    # if=, of=: the file is embedded in a KEY=VALUE word that PaSh cannot rewrite to a fifo, so we only
    #   parallelize when the data flows through stdin and stdout.
    # count=, skip=/iseek=, seek=/oseek=: select a byte range of the whole stream -> not parallelizable.
    # conv=: lcase/ucase are per-byte maps and keep the property; noerror, fsync, fdatasync, excl,
    #   nocreat, notrunc, sparse only change how the output is opened/flushed. Everything else
    #   (ascii/ebcdic/ibm with cbs, block/unblock, swab, sync) works on record or block boundaries
    #   that depend on how the stream is cut -> not parallelizable.
    # bs=, ibs=, obs=, cbs= (without block/unblock), iflag=, oflag=, status= do not change the bytes
    #   produced.

    _CONV_SYMBOLS_KEEPING_BYTE_MAP = {
        "lcase", "ucase", "noerror", "fsync", "fdatasync", "excl", "nocreat", "notrunc", "sparse",
    }

    def _parse_key_value_operands(self):
        keys_given: Set[str] = set()
        list_symbols: Dict[str, Set[str]] = {"conv": set(), "iflag": set(), "oflag": set()}
        for operand in self.cmd_inv.operand_list:
            word = str(operand.get_name())
            if "=" not in word:
                continue
            key, value = word.split("=", 1)
            if key == "oseek":
                key = "seek"
            elif key == "iseek":
                key = "skip"
            keys_given.add(key)
            if key in list_symbols:
                list_symbols[key].update(s for s in value.split(",") if s != "")
        return keys_given, list_symbols

    def generate_info(self) -> None:
        if self.does_flag_option_list_contain_at_least_one_of(["--help", "--version"]):
            return
        keys_given, list_symbols = self._parse_key_value_operands()
        if keys_given & {"if", "of", "count", "skip", "seek"}:
            return
        if not list_symbols["conv"] <= self._CONV_SYMBOLS_KEEPING_BYTE_MAP:
            return
        self.append_to_parallelizer_list_cc_seq_conc()
        self.append_to_parallelizer_list_rr_seq_conc()

    # same dd on each and concatenating the results gives the same bytes: CC/RR x SEQ x CONC.

All four deliverables are written under `output/` and tested against the real `/usr/bin/dd` (coreutils 9.4) and against the real `pash_annotations` package.

## What I produced

**`output/dd.py`** — the syntax description. `dd` has no positional operands; everything is a `KEY=VALUE` word, so each key is modelled as an option with `flag_followed_by_equals=True`, and the positional list is empty. `if`/`of` are `Path`; `bs`/`cbs`/`ibs`/`obs` are `Size`; `count`, `skip` (alias `iseek`) and `seek` (alias `oseek`) are `Integer(min=0, suffixes=...)`; `conv`/`iflag`/`oflag` are comma-separated `List`s of `Selection`; `status` is a `Selection`; plus the `--help`/`--version` flags.

**`output/annotation/`** — the PaSh annotation:
- `dd.json` lists `--help`/`--version` as flags and an empty `option` list. PaSh's parser only matches whole words and never splits `key=value`, so listing `if` etc. as options would be wrong; I documented the key=value table under an extra, parser-ignored `key_value_operand` key (there's precedent for extra keys in PaSh's own `export.json`).
- `InputOutputInfoGeneratorDd.py` parses the `key=value` operands itself, marks all of them as non-file config strings, and reports the `if=` file (or stdin) and `of=` file (or stdout) through the implicit streaming input/output slots. The output file is marked `OTHER_OUTPUT` instead of `STREAM_OUTPUT` when `seek`/`oseek` is non-zero, `conv=notrunc`, or `oflag=append`, since existing file contents are then preserved.
- `ParallelizabilityInfoGeneratorDd.py` offers consecutive-chunks and round-robin splitting with plain concatenation, only when data flows stdin→stdout (no `if=`/`of=`), no `count`/`skip`/`seek`, and `conv` is limited to byte-wise or open-mode symbols.

## What I verified against the binary
- Repeated keys: last one wins, but `conv`/`iflag`/`oflag` accumulate across repeats.
- `if=-` / `of=-` are literal filenames, not stdin/stdout — the generator deliberately doesn't map `-`.
- `--help`/`--version` win wherever they appear (even after `bs=1`); the generators also catch them when PaSh's parser has left them in the operand list.
- `fullblock` is accepted for `iflag` only; `count_bytes`/`skip_bytes`/`seek_bytes` are accepted (undocumented), so the `iflag`/`oflag` choice lists differ. `B` suffix works on `bs=` too, so one suffix list is used.
- An automated check loaded `dd.py` and tried every option, alias, choice, and suffix on the binary: 0 mismatches, and the spec's key set equals the set in `dd --help`.
- Parallelism: splitting a 270 KB file and concatenating per-chunk `dd` outputs matched the sequential output byte-for-byte for every annotated-parallelisable case, and differed for `count`, `skip`, `conv=sync`, `conv=unblock`, and — with odd-sized chunks — `conv=swab`, `conv=block`, and `conv=ebcdic cbs=…` (while `conv=ebcdic` without `cbs` matched, which is why those three are allowed only when `cbs=` is absent).

## Things I'm unsure about
- `caruca` is not on PyPI and not on this machine, so `dd.py` was only validated with a stub module that accepts the documented keyword arguments. In particular I assumed `suffixes=` takes a tuple of suffix strings and that `List(of=Selection(...), separator=",")` is the right spelling for comma-lists; adjust if the real constructors differ.
- Reporting `of=FILE` via the implicit-output slot is the only way to name the file without `of=` baked into the name, but PaSh's `has_other_outputs()` only inspects operand/option typers, so an `of=` with `seek`/`notrunc`/`append` won't trip that particular side-effect check (the access kind on the slot is `OTHER_OUTPUT`, and no parallelizers are offered in those cases, so nothing unsound follows).
- Z/Y/R/Q suffixes are syntactically parsed by `dd` but overflow 64 bits at runtime; I kept them in the spec since the manual lists them.
- Non-parallel annotations are conservative for `conv=swab`, `block`, `unblock`, `sync`; the `status=` key affects only stderr and is ignored.

The output file is marked `OTHER_OUTPUT` instead of `STREAM_OUTPUT` when `seek`/`oseek` is non-zero, `conv=notrunc`, or `oflag=append`, since existing file contents are then preserved.
- `ParallelizabilityInfoGeneratorDd.py` offers consecutive-chunks and round-robin splitting with plain concatenation, only when data flows stdin→stdout (no `if=`/`of=`), no `count`/`skip`/`seek`, and `conv` is limited to byte-wise or open-mode symbols.

## What I verified against the binary
- Repeated keys: last one wins, but `conv`/`iflag`/`oflag` accumulate across repeats.
- `if=-` / `of=-` are literal filenames, not stdin/stdout — the generator deliberately doesn't map `-`.
- `--help`/`--version` win wherever they appear (even after `bs=1`); the generators also catch them when PaSh's parser has left them in the operand list.
- `fullblock` is accepted for `iflag` only; `count_bytes`/`skip_bytes`/`seek_bytes` are accepted (undocumented), so the `iflag`/`oflag` choice lists differ. `B` suffix works on `bs=` too, so one suffix list is used.
- An automated check loaded `dd.py` and tried every option, alias, choice, and suffix on the binary: 0 mismatches, and the spec's key set equals the set in `dd --help`.
- Parallelism: splitting a 270 KB file and concatenating per-chunk `dd` outputs matched the sequential output byte-for-byte for every annotated-parallelisable case, and differed for `count`, `skip`, `conv=sync`, `conv=unblock`, and — with odd-sized chunks — `conv=swab`, `conv=block`, and `conv=ebcdic cbs=…` (while `conv=ebcdic` without `cbs` matched, which is why those three are allowed only when `cbs=` is absent).

## Things I'm unsure about
- `caruca` is not on PyPI and not on this machine, so `dd.py` was only validated with a stub module that accepts the documented keyword arguments. In particular I assumed `suffixes=` takes a tuple of suffix strings and that `List(of=Selection(...), separator=",")` is the right spelling for comma-lists; adjust if the real constructors differ.
- Reporting `of=FILE` via the implicit-output slot is the only way to name the file without `of=` baked into the name, but PaSh's `has_other_outputs()` only inspects operand/option typers, so an `of=` with `seek`/`notrunc`/`append` won't trip that particular side-effect check (the access kind on the slot is `OTHER_OUTPUT`, and no parallelizers are offered in those cases, so nothing unsound follows).
- Z/Y/R/Q suffixes are syntactically parsed by `dd` but overflow 64 bits at runtime; I kept them in the spec since the manual lists them.
- Non-parallel annotations are conservative for `conv=swab`, `block`, `unblock`, `sync`; the `status=` key affects only stderr and is ignored.
